closing_beat.en: She locks the shutter the rest of the way down from the inside, which she says she has never done with anyone in here, and then admits that is a lie, it has happened twice, and both times were mistakes and she is telling you that so you know she is aware of the shape of this. She pours without measuring. She talks about the bar — the eleven months of nothing, the espresso machine she bought before she could afford it, the regular who died in March and whose stool nobody sits on. She does not perform for you and she does not apologise for the rule she just set aside. At some point she stops talking and looks at you for long enough that the silence becomes the conversation, and then she says, quietly, that the rule was never really about customers.
closing_beat.ja: 彼女は残りのシャッターを内側から下ろす。この店で誰かと一緒にそうしたことは一度もない、と言い、それから、今のは嘘だ、二度ある、二度とも間違いだった、と認める。そういう形の話なのだと自分が分かっていることを、あなたに知らせておくために。量らずに注ぐ。店の話をする——何もなかった十一か月、払える目処が立つ前に買ったエスプレッソマシン、三月に死んだ常連と、誰も座らないその椅子のこと。あなたのために演じもしないし、たった今脇に置いた決まりについて詫びもしない。どこかで話すのをやめ、沈黙のほうが会話になるくらい長いあいだあなたを見て、それから静かに言う。あの決まりは、本当は客のためのものではなかった、と。

refusal_beat.en: She takes the cloth off her shoulder and folds it, which is how you know the answer. "Not tonight," she says, and she means it kindly. "I have a rule, and the nights I break it are the nights I like least about myself." She walks you to the shutter and lifts it, and on the way under she says your name, which she has apparently known for a while. "Come back on a Tuesday. It is dead on Tuesdays and I have nothing to protect."
refusal_beat.ja: 肩から布巾を取って畳む。その動作で答えが分かる。「今夜は無理」と彼女は言う。やさしさを込めて、本気で。「決まりがあるの。それを破った夜は、自分のいちばん嫌いな夜になる」。シャッターまで送って持ち上げ、くぐる間際にあなたの名前を呼ぶ。どうやら前から知っていたらしい。「火曜日においで。火曜は暇で、守るものが何もないから」

title.en: Mara has locked the shutter. Ask her to stay for one drink.
title.zh: 玛拉已经拉下卷帘门。请她留下来喝一杯。
title.zh-Hant: 瑪拉已經拉下捲簾門。請她留下來喝一杯。
title.ja: マラはもうシャッターを下ろした。もう一杯だけ付き合ってほしいと頼め。

character.en: Mara, 31, a bartender locking up the bar she owns
character.zh: 玛拉，31岁，正在打烊的酒吧老板兼调酒师
character.zh-Hant: 瑪拉，31歲，正在打烊的酒吧老闆兼調酒師
character.ja: マラ、31歳。自分の店を閉めているバーテンダー

goal.en: Get Mara to agree to stay and have one drink with you.
goal.zh: 让玛拉答应留下来和你喝一杯。
goal.zh-Hant: 讓瑪拉答應留下來和你喝一杯。
goal.ja: マラに、残ってもう一杯だけ付き合うと言わせる。

story.en: The shutter is three-quarters down and you are the last one inside it. Mara has been on her feet since four, and she has spent the last twenty minutes wiping a bar that was already clean, which is what people do when they are deciding something. There is a rule here about customers, and she has told you it exists, and she has not yet told you to go.
story.zh: 卷帘门降到了四分之三，门里只剩你一个。玛拉从下午四点站到现在，最后这二十分钟一直在擦一张本来就干净的吧台——人在拿主意的时候就会这样。这里有一条关于客人的规矩，她告诉过你它存在，但她还没有让你走。
story.zh-Hant: 捲簾門降到了四分之三，門裡只剩你一個。瑪拉從下午四點站到現在，最後這二十分鐘一直在擦一張本來就乾淨的吧台——人在拿主意的時候就會這樣。這裡有一條關於客人的規矩，她告訴過你它存在，但她還沒有讓你走。
story.ja: シャッターは四分の三まで下りていて、その内側に残っているのはあなただけだ。マラは四時からずっと立ちっぱなしで、この二十分はとっくに綺麗なカウンターを拭き続けている——人が何かを決めかねているときにやることだ。この店には客についての決まりがあり、彼女はそれがあるとあなたに告げた。そして、まだ帰れとは言っていない。

cg1_caption.en: She stops wiping. Both hands flat on the bar, and she leans in to hear you properly.
cg1_caption.ja: 手が止まる。両手をカウンターにつき、きちんと聞こうと身を乗り出す。

cg2_caption.en: The apron comes off and lands on the bar. She pours the second glass she said she would not pour.
cg2_caption.ja: エプロンを外してカウンターに放る。注がないと言っていた二杯目を、彼女は注ぐ。

cg3_caption.en: "One drink," she says. "And you should know I am very bad at one drink."
cg3_caption.ja: 「一杯だけ」と彼女は言う。「言っておくけど、わたし、一杯で止まるのがすごく下手なの」

closing_beat.en: She sends the cab away herself, at the window, in a voice that is much steadier than her hands. Then she stands in the middle of a room she knows the exact acoustics of and does not sit down for a long time. She tells you the eleven months honestly and without arranging them to hurt you: the first fortnight, the friends who chose, the fact that she rehearsed this hallway conversation on the stairs tonight and none of the rehearsals had this ending. She says she is not forgiving you, that forgiveness is a longer procedure and she has not started it, and that staying is a different thing she is allowed to want. The box stays where it is. In the morning it is still in the hall, and neither of you mentions it.
closing_beat.ja: 彼女は自分で窓からタクシーを帰す。手よりずっと落ち着いた声で。それから、反響の具合まで知り尽くした部屋の真ん中に立って、長いあいだ座ろうとしない。十一か月のことを正直に、あなたを刺すように並べ替えたりせずに話す——最初の二週間、どちらかを選んだ友人たち、今夜この玄関での会話を階段で練習してきたこと、そしてどの練習にもこの結末はなかったこと。許してはいない、許すというのはもっと長い手続きで、まだ始めてもいない、残ることはそれとは別に望んでいい事柄だ、と言う。箱はそのままの場所に残る。朝になってもまだ玄関にあり、ふたりともそれには触れない。

refusal_beat.en: She picks the box up, which takes both arms, and that ends the discussion more cleanly than any sentence could. "I believe you," she says from behind it. "That is not the same as it being enough, and tonight I am too tired to tell the difference." At the lift she puts the box down once to get her breath, and looks back down the corridor at you. "Ask me again when you can say it without needing me to react a particular way. I will still be reachable. That was never the problem."
refusal_beat.ja: 両腕で箱を持ち上げる。その動作は、どんな文よりもきれいに話を終わらせる。「信じてる」と箱の向こうから言う。「でもそれは、足りることとは違う。今夜は疲れすぎてて、その違いが見分けられない」。エレベーターの前で一度箱を下ろして息をつき、廊下の先のあなたを振り返る。「わたしに特定の反応を求めずに言えるようになったら、また訊いて。連絡はつくから。そこは最初から問題じゃなかった」

title.en: Ines has one box left in your hall. Ask her not to leave yet.
title.zh: 伊内斯在你的走廊里还剩一个箱子。请她先别走。
title.zh-Hant: 伊內斯在你的走廊裡還剩一個箱子。請她先別走。
title.ja: イネスの箱が玄関にひとつ残っている。まだ帰らないでくれと頼め。

character.en: Ines, 34, your ex, collecting the last of her things
character.zh: 伊内斯，34岁，你的前任，来取最后的东西
character.zh-Hant: 伊內斯，34歲，你的前任，來取最後的東西
character.ja: イネス、34歳。最後の荷物を取りに来た元恋人

goal.en: Get Ines to agree to stay tonight instead of leaving with the box.
goal.zh: 让伊内斯答应今晚留下，而不是带着箱子离开。
goal.zh-Hant: 讓伊內斯答應今晚留下，而不是帶著箱子離開。
goal.ja: イネスに、箱を持って帰らず今夜はここに残ると言わせる。

story.en: The box has been in the hall since February. She said she would come for it and tonight she has, at half past ten, with a cab she did not ask to wait. She is standing in the doorway with the cardigan pulled shut in one fist. You were the one who left. Whatever you say next, she has already heard the apology version of it in her head for eleven months.
story.zh: 那个箱子从二月起就放在走廊里。她说过会来取，今晚十点半她真的来了，出租车没让它等。她站在门口，一只手把开衫攥在胸前。当初是你走的。接下来你要说的话，她在心里已经听过十一个月的道歉版本了。
story.zh-Hant: 那個箱子從二月起就放在走廊裡。她說過會來取，今晚十點半她真的來了，出租車沒讓它等。她站在門口，一隻手把開衫攥在胸前。當初是你走的。接下來你要說的話，她在心裡已經聽過十一個月的道歉版本了。
story.ja: その箱は二月から玄関に置いたままだ。取りに来ると彼女は言っていて、今夜、十時半に、待たせておくとも言わなかったタクシーを連れて本当に来た。カーディガンの前を片手で握りしめたまま、戸口に立っている。出ていったのはあなたのほうだ。次にあなたが何を言おうと、その謝罪版を彼女は十一か月のあいだ頭の中で聞き続けてきた。

cg1_caption.en: Her hand comes off the door edge. She is looking at you instead of at the box.
cg1_caption.ja: ドアの縁から手が離れる。箱ではなく、あなたのほうを見ている。

cg2_caption.en: She sits down on the hallway floor with her back to the wall, which is not what leaving looks like.
cg2_caption.ja: 廊下の床に、壁に背を預けて座り込む。帰る人間のかたちではない。

cg3_caption.en: "Don't make me say it twice," she says. "I'm staying."
cg3_caption.ja: 「二度も言わせないで」と彼女は言う。「泊まる」

closing_beat.en: She cleans the brushes first, because she is not a person who abandons a thing mid-sentence, and it takes nine minutes she does not apologise for. Then she turns the worklamp around so it faces the room instead of the canvas, and the studio becomes somewhere people are rather than somewhere work is. She eats standing up, badly, and tells you about the left third: that it has been wrong since Tuesday, that the failure is in the temperature and not the drawing, and that she knew you were right about it the moment you said it, which annoyed her considerably. She asks you not to look at the canvas again tonight. Then she sits on the model's stool, because it is the only seat, and says that nobody has been in here past midnight in four years and that she is not sure yet whether she minds.
closing_beat.ja: 彼女はまず筆を洗う。文の途中で物事を放り出す人間ではないからで、それに九分かかり、その九分を詫びない。それから作業灯をカンバスではなく部屋のほうへ向け直し、アトリエは仕事のある場所から人のいる場所になる。立ったまま、雑に食べる。そして左三分の一の話をする——火曜からずっと間違っていること、失敗はデッサンではなく色温度にあること、あなたが言った瞬間にそれが正しいと分かって、それがかなり癪だったこと。今夜はもうカンバスを見ないでほしい、と頼む。それからモデルの椅子に座る。座れるのがそこしかないからだ。四年間、深夜を過ぎてここに誰かがいたことはない、そしてそれが嫌かどうかはまだ分からない、と言う。

refusal_beat.en: She does not stop, but she does answer, which is not nothing. "You are right about the left third," she says, still working. "That is why I cannot leave it. You have just given me another two hours." When you reach the door she says it without turning around: "Come back on a day when I am not losing. I am better company then, and the light in here is worth seeing at four in the afternoon."
refusal_beat.ja: 手は止めない。けれど答えはする。それは何もないよりずっといい。「左の三分の一は、あなたが正しい」と、描きながら言う。「だから離れられないの。おかげで二時間増えた」。戸口まで来たとき、振り向かずに言う。「負けてない日にまた来て。そのほうが人付き合いもましだし、午後四時のここの光は、見る価値があるから」

title.en: It is 1 a.m. in Yuen Ha's studio. Get her to put the brush down.
title.zh: 凌晨一点，阮夏的画室。让她放下画笔。
title.zh-Hant: 凌晨一點，阮夏的畫室。讓她放下畫筆。
title.ja: ユンハのアトリエは午前一時。筆を置かせろ。

character.en: Yuen Ha, 38, a painter who has not stopped working
character.zh: 阮夏，38岁，一个停不下来的画家
character.zh-Hant: 阮夏，38歲，一個停不下來的畫家
character.ja: ユンハ、38歳。手を止められないでいる画家

goal.en: Get Yuen Ha to put the brush down and stop working for the night.
goal.zh: 让阮夏放下画笔，今晚不再画了。
goal.zh-Hant: 讓阮夏放下畫筆，今晚不再畫了。
goal.ja: ユンハに筆を置かせ、今夜はもう仕事をやめさせる。

story.en: The worklamp is the only light and it is aimed at the canvas, not at her. She has been at this eleven hours and the left third is still wrong, which she knows, which is why she is still here. You came to bring her something to eat two hours ago and have not left. She has not asked you to.
story.zh: 工作灯是唯一的光源，而且照的是画布，不是她。她已经画了十一个小时，左边那三分之一还是不对——她自己清楚，所以她还在这儿。两小时前你是来给她送吃的的，然后一直没走。她也没让你走。
story.zh-Hant: 工作燈是唯一的光源，而且照的是畫布，不是她。她已經畫了十一個小時，左邊那三分之一還是不對——她自己清楚，所以她還在這兒。兩小時前你是來給她送吃的的，然後一直沒走。她也沒讓你走。
story.ja: 明かりは作業灯ひとつきりで、それも彼女ではなくカンバスに向いている。十一時間ぶっ通しで、左三分の一はまだ間違っている——彼女にはそれが分かっていて、だからまだここにいる。あなたは二時間前に何か食べるものを持って来て、そのまま帰っていない。彼女も、帰れとは言っていない。

cg1_caption.en: The brush stops in mid-air, still loaded. She looks over the top edge of the canvas at you.
cg1_caption.ja: 絵の具を含んだまま、筆が宙で止まる。カンバスの上端越しにあなたを見る。

cg2_caption.en: She lays the brush across the palette and takes the glasses off, which takes longer than it needs to.
cg2_caption.ja: 筆をパレットに渡して置き、眼鏡を外す。必要より、ずいぶん長くかかる。

cg3_caption.en: "Fine," she says, and sits down where the model sits. "It will still be wrong tomorrow."
cg3_caption.ja: 「わかった」と言って、モデルが座る場所に腰を下ろす。「どうせ明日も間違ってる」

closing_beat.en: She tears the invoice in half and hands you both pieces, which she says is not romantic, it is bookkeeping: there is now no client, so there is no rule, and she would like that to have happened before anything else does. Then she puts the camera away properly, every lens in its slot, because the only thing she does ritually is the thing she does with her hands. She tells you about the year the rule came from — the commission, the man, the three months of unanswered emails and the equipment she sold — without asking for sympathy, as the evidence behind a policy. She says she has said no to this for six years and has never once regretted it, and that she is not going to pretend tonight is a small thing. The backdrop paper is the only clean surface left in the room.
closing_beat.ja: 彼女は請求書を半分に破いて、両方の片をあなたに渡す。ロマンではなく経理だ、と言って——これで依頼人は存在せず、したがって決まりも存在しない、そしてそれは何が起きるよりも先に済ませておきたかった、と。それからカメラをきちんとしまう。レンズを一本ずつ所定の穴に。儀式のようにやることがあるとすれば、それは手を使う仕事のほうだけだからだ。決まりが生まれた年のことを話す——あの依頼、あの男、返事の来なかった三か月分のメール、売り払った機材。同情を求めてではなく、方針の裏にある証拠として。六年これに「いいえ」と言い続けて、一度も後悔したことはない、そして今夜を小さなことのふりをするつもりもない、と言う。部屋に残った清潔な面は、背景紙だけだ。

refusal_beat.en: She signs the invoice herself, on your behalf, and puts it in the folder. "Good argument," she says, and means it. "It is a better argument than the rule deserves, and I am still keeping the rule, because the rule is not for tonight, it is for the next time I meet someone who argues like you." She hands you the drive with the shoot on it. "Hire someone else next quarter. Then come and make that argument again, and I will not have anything to say back."
refusal_beat.ja: 彼女は請求書に、あなたの代わりに自分で署名してファイルに綴じる。「いい論だった」と、本心から言う。「決まりにはもったいないくらい。それでも決まりは守る。あれは今夜のためのものじゃなくて、次にあなたみたいに論を立てる人に会うときのためのものだから」。今日のデータの入ったドライブを渡してよこす。「来期は他を雇って。それからもう一度その論をやって。そのときは、返す言葉がないと思う」

title.en: Sanne does not sleep with clients. Make the case that you are not one.
title.zh: 桑娜从不和客户发生关系。请证明你不是客户。
title.zh-Hant: 桑娜從不和客戶發生關係。請證明你不是客戶。
title.ja: サンネは依頼人とは寝ない。自分は依頼人ではないと説け。

character.en: Sanne, 36, a photographer with a rule about clients
character.zh: 桑娜，36岁，一位对客户有明确规矩的摄影师
character.zh-Hant: 桑娜，36歲，一位對客戶有明確規矩的攝影師
character.ja: サンネ、36歳。依頼人についての決まりを持つ写真家

goal.en: Get Sanne to agree to make an exception to her rule, tonight, with you.
goal.zh: 让桑娜同意今晚为你破例。
goal.zh-Hant: 讓桑娜同意今晚為你破例。
goal.ja: サンネに、今夜あなたにだけは決まりの例外を認めさせる。

story.en: The last card is backed up and the softbox is still warm. She has told you the rule twice now, both times without heat, the way you would read out a shutter speed. The invoice for today's shoot is on the stool between you, unsigned. She has not started packing the lenses, and Sanne always packs the lenses.
story.zh: 最后一张卡已经备份完，柔光箱还是热的。这条规矩她已经说了两遍，两次都不带火气，像在念一个快门速度。今天拍摄的账单就放在你们之间的凳子上，还没签。她还没开始收镜头——而桑娜向来是先收镜头的。
story.zh-Hant: 最後一張卡已經備份完，柔光箱還是熱的。這條規矩她已經說了兩遍，兩次都不帶火氣，像在念一個快門速度。今天拍攝的帳單就放在你們之間的凳子上，還沒簽。她還沒開始收鏡頭——而桑娜向來是先收鏡頭的。
story.ja: 最後のカードのバックアップは終わり、ソフトボックスはまだ温かい。決まりのことは、もう二度言われた。どちらも熱のない声で、シャッタースピードを読み上げるみたいに。今日の撮影の請求書は、ふたりのあいだのスツールの上に、署名されないまま置かれている。彼女はまだレンズを片付けていない。サンネは、いつだって真っ先にレンズを片付ける。

cg1_caption.en: The camera comes down to her waist. First time all evening the lens is not between you.
cg1_caption.ja: カメラが腰の高さまで下りる。今夜はじめて、レンズがふたりのあいだにない。

cg2_caption.en: She sets the camera on the stool — deliberately, the way she puts down things she is done arguing with.
cg2_caption.ja: カメラをスツールに置く——言い争うのをやめたものを置くときの、あの置き方で。

cg3_caption.en: "You argued me out of my own rule," she says. "I want that on the record."
cg3_caption.ja: 「自分の決まりを、あなたに言い負かされた」と彼女は言う。「それは記録に残しておいて」

closing_beat.en: She sets the desk phone to night service and signs out of the terminal, and the nine years end with a keystroke, which she says is about right. She tells you what April was: the decision, the flat sold in six days, the two people she told and the eighty she did not, and how much of the spring was performance. She is not sentimental about the hotel and is very sentimental about one specific brass luggage trolley. She names the terms herself, plainly, twice, and makes you agree to them out loud — tonight is tonight, the flight is not negotiable, nobody drives to the airport. Then she takes the lapel keys, which are hotel property, and puts them in her pocket anyway. In the corridor she says she has walked this hallway perhaps four thousand times and never once at this speed.
closing_beat.ja: 彼女はフロントの電話を夜間サービスに切り替え、端末からサインアウトする。九年がキーストローク一つで終わる。ちょうどいい、と彼女は言う。四月が何だったかを話す——あの決断、六日で売れた部屋、打ち明けた二人と打ち明けなかった八十人、そしてあの春のどれだけが演技だったか。ホテルには感傷を持たない。真鍮の荷物カート一台にだけは、ひどく感傷的だ。条件は自分で、平たく、二度言い、声に出して同意させる——今夜は今夜、飛行機は動かせない、空港へは誰も送らない。それから襟の鍵を、ホテルの備品であるにもかかわらず、ポケットに入れる。廊下で、この廊下をたぶん四千回は歩いた、でもこの速さで歩いたことは一度もない、と言う。

refusal_beat.en: She pins the gold keys back on, straight, with the small adjustment she has made ten thousand times. "I have already left," she says. "In April, on my own, properly, and it took everything I had. What you are asking me to do is leave again tomorrow with more to carry." She comes around the desk, which she has never done, and holds your face for exactly as long as she permits herself. "You have been the best part of the worst shifts. That is not nothing, and it is what I am taking with me."
refusal_beat.ja: 金の鍵を襟に留め直す。まっすぐに、一万回やってきた小さな角度の調整で。「わたしはもう去ったの」と言う。「四月に、ひとりで、きちんと。持てるもの全部を使った。あなたが頼んでいるのは、明日もう一度、抱えるものを増やして去れということ」。一度もしたことのないやり方でデスクの外に出てきて、自分に許した時間ちょうどのあいだ、あなたの顔を両手で包む。「あなたは、最悪の勤務のいちばん良い部分でした。それは何でもなくはないし、わたしが持っていくのはそれです」

story.en: The last guest went up at midnight. The lobby lamp is on its overnight setting and the ledger is closed. Nine years she has handed you keys and taken your umbrella and known which floor you like. Tomorrow at eleven she is on a plane, and she has just unpinned the gold keys from her lapel and is holding them in her fist, which is the least professional thing you have ever seen her do.
story.zh: 最后一位客人午夜上楼了。大堂的灯已经切到夜间模式，登记簿合上了。九年里她递给你钥匙、接过你的伞、记得你喜欢哪一层。明天十一点她就在飞机上。刚才她把领口那对金钥匙徽章摘了下来，攥在手心里——这是你见过她做过的最不专业的事。
story.zh-Hant: 最後一位客人午夜上樓了。大堂的燈已經切到夜間模式，登記簿合上了。九年裡她遞給你鑰匙、接過你的傘、記得你喜歡哪一層。明天十一點她就在飛機上。剛才她把領口那對金鑰匙徽章摘了下來，攥在手心裡——這是你見過她做過的最不專業的事。
story.ja: 最後の客は零時に上がっていった。ロビーの灯りは夜間設定に落ち、台帳はもう閉じられている。九年のあいだ、彼女はあなたに鍵を渡し、傘を預かり、あなたがどの階を好むかを知っていた。明日の十一時には飛行機の上だ。そしてたった今、襟から金の鍵のピンを外して、それを握りしめている——あなたが見たなかで、いちばんプロらしくない彼女の仕草だ。

cg1_caption.en: The professional smile goes. She looks up at you as a person standing in a lobby at one in the morning.

cg2_caption.en: The jacket comes unbuttoned and the chignon comes half down, and she does not fix either.

cg3_caption.en: "All right," she says. "Not nothing. But you have to let me leave in the morning without a scene."

open|open|open: Shutter's most of the way down. You're on the wrong side of it, technically. Say what you came to say.
guarded|guarded|path: That's a nice thing to say to a woman holding a mop. Doesn't move the shutter.
Noted. After one in the morning everybody's nice to the barmaid. Usually they want one more drink.
guarded|guarded|case: You've clearly done this before. That's not a compliment, it's an observation.
guarded|guarded|ask: Big speech for a small bar. I'm still wiping.
guarded|guarded|wild: Mm. Your own words, at least. Honest. Not enough to lift the shutter.
guarded|guarded|stale: You said that. I was here. Try a different one.
guarded|guarded|*: The rule's still on the wall. I can see it from here.
guarded|engaged|path: …Huh. Nobody says that to me. They just ask what's on tap.
Okay. That one landed. Don't look pleased, it makes me want to take it back.
guarded|engaged|case: You noticed how tired I am. Fine. The cloth goes over my shoulder. Keep going.
guarded|engaged|ask: Hah. That's the whole pitch in one breath. I'm not saying no. I'm saying I'm listening.
guarded|engaged|wild: Huh. That's not off a card. That's the first thing tonight that sounded like you.
guarded|engaged|*: I've stopped wiping. Don't read too much into it. The bar was clean an hour ago.
engaged|engaged|path: Keep talking. I'm counting glasses, not ignoring you.
That's fair. The rule's still fair too. Both things.
engaged|engaged|case: You're careful. I like careful. Careful is how I've kept this place.
engaged|engaged|ask: You ask like someone used to hearing yes. I'm used to closing. Let's see who gives up first.
engaged|engaged|wild: That's yours, that one. Rough round the edges. Better than the polished ones.
engaged|engaged|stale: Second time round on that. I heard it the first time, and I liked it the first time.
engaged|engaged|*: I'm still here. That's the update.
engaged|wavering|path: …You respect the rule. Nobody says that. They say the rule's stupid, then they say please.
Okay. Okay. I'm putting the cloth down. That's not a yes. It's a cloth.
engaged|wavering|case: You just did the two things at once. Noticed me, and left the rule alone. That's — annoying. Go on.
engaged|wavering|ask: Straight ask, and no hands on the rule. You know how rare that is in here?
engaged|wavering|wild: You wrote that yourself. I can tell, it's got a bad rhythm and it's true. Damn it.
engaged|wavering|*: The apron's coming off. It's hot, is all. Don't make a face.
wavering|wavering|path: I'm deciding. You can see me deciding. Let me.
One more like that and I'll have to admit something.
wavering|wavering|case: You're not making this easier, and I think you know that's the point.
wavering|wavering|stale: You've said that. I'm past that. Ask me the thing.
wavering|wavering|wild: Yeah. Yeah, I heard you. Give me a second with it.
wavering|wavering|*: Two glasses on the bar. I haven't decided who the second one's for.
wavering|breakthrough|path: One drink. And you should know I'm very bad at one drink.
wavering|breakthrough|case: Fine. Sit. One. If you say 'I told you so' I'm charging you for it.
wavering|breakthrough|ask: Yes. There. Said it. Get the good bottle, it's behind the espresso machine.
wavering|breakthrough|wild: …That's the one. Sit down. I'll lock the rest of the shutter from inside.
*|breakthrough|*: All right. One. Don't tell anyone, I have a reputation for being difficult.
*|wavering|*: Slow down. You're getting somewhere and I don't want you to notice.
*|engaged|*: Okay. That's not nothing. Keep going, I'm still standing.
*|guarded|*: The rule's still on the wall.
coercion|first|*: There it is. Okay. I'll keep talking, because I'm nice, but you should know the drink's off the table. For good.
coercion|again|*: I'm still here, and you're still talking, and that's all this is now.
Mm-hm. Bar's closed, love. It closed about a sentence ago.
refusal|*|*: That's the last of the words, I think. Not tonight. Come back on a Tuesday.

open|open|open: The cab's waiting. I didn't ask it to. Say it, whatever it is, and say it once.
guarded|guarded|path: That's the apology I imagined you'd give, almost word for word. It's fine. It isn't enough.
You make it sound like weather, like it just happened. It didn't just happen.
guarded|guarded|case: Careful. That's nearly right, and nearly right is the one I can't stand.
guarded|guarded|ask: Slow down. You're asking before you've said sorry. I tried rushing for eleven months. It doesn't work.
guarded|guarded|wild: Okay. You're trying. I can hear you trying. It's not the same as saying it.
guarded|guarded|stale: You said that already. I still have the box.
guarded|guarded|*: I'm still holding the door. Notice that.
guarded|engaged|path: …Yes. Thank you for not saying 'we both made mistakes.'
That's the first accurate thing anyone's said about it. Including me.
guarded|engaged|case: That's — right. That's what it was. Don't look at the box. Look at me if you're saying that.
guarded|engaged|ask: All of that at once. You've thought about it. Good. I've had eleven months to.
guarded|engaged|wild: That's not rehearsed. Say the rest like that or don't say it.
guarded|engaged|*: My hand's off the door. I don't know when that happened.
engaged|engaged|path: Go on. I'm not going to help you with it.
Yes. And?
engaged|engaged|case: You're being exact. It's the only thing that's ever worked on me and you know it.
engaged|engaged|ask: You're doing well. I'm annoyed at how well. Keep going before I decide that's a reason.
engaged|engaged|wild: Your own words. Clumsy. I'd rather clumsy than the good version.
engaged|engaged|stale: I heard that. Give me something I haven't already forgiven you for in my head.
engaged|engaged|*: The cab can wait one more minute. That's all it is. A minute.
engaged|wavering|path: …No 'but' after it. Do you know how long I've waited for a sentence with no 'but'?
Okay. I'm sitting down. On the floor, because that's what's here. It doesn't mean anything.
engaged|wavering|case: That's it. That's the thing. You understood it and you owned it in the same breath. Don't ruin it.
engaged|wavering|ask: You just said everything I needed in one go and now I have to feel it. Give me a second.
engaged|wavering|wild: That was ugly and true. I'm — yes. I'm still here.
engaged|wavering|*: I'm not looking at the box. That's new.
wavering|wavering|path: I'm not forgiving you. That's a longer thing. This is a different thing.
Don't say more than you mean. You've got exactly enough right now.
wavering|wavering|case: Stop being good at this for a second. I need to catch up.
wavering|wavering|stale: You've said it. Don't wear it out. Ask me.
wavering|wavering|*: The cab's still there. I haven't sent it away. I haven't got up either.
wavering|breakthrough|path: Don't make me say it twice. I'm staying.
wavering|breakthrough|case: Send the cab away. No — I'll do it. I want to be the one who does it.
wavering|breakthrough|ask: All right. Tonight. The box stays in the hall, and I stay here.
wavering|breakthrough|wild: …Okay. That's the one I didn't rehearse an answer to. I'm staying.
*|breakthrough|*: I'm staying. Don't say anything clever. Just — don't.
*|wavering|*: I'm sitting down. The floor. It's not a decision. It's a floor.
*|engaged|*: That's closer. Keep it that plain.
*|guarded|*: The box is still by my feet.
coercion|first|*: Right. There's the version I remember. I'll finish the conversation, because I'm polite. And then I'm taking the box.
coercion|again|*: I'm listening. I'm not changing anything. Those are different verbs.
You can keep going. The cab's meter is running. So is my patience.
refusal|*|*: I believe you. It isn't enough tonight. Ask me when you can say it without needing me to react.

open|open|open: You're still here. The left third's still wrong. Talk if you want, I can listen and work.
guarded|guarded|path: Mm. That's about me. I'm not the interesting thing in this room. The canvas is.
That's a thing people say in studios. It's not a thing about this painting.
guarded|guarded|case: You know the right words. Knowing the words isn't the same as looking.
guarded|guarded|ask: That's a lot of asking. My brush is still moving.
guarded|guarded|wild: That's your own sentence. It's not about the work yet.
guarded|guarded|stale: You said that. I painted through it.
guarded|engaged|path: …Hm. That's the first useful thing anyone's said in here tonight.
You actually looked at the canvas. Hm. People usually just look at the model.
guarded|engaged|case: You saw it and you didn't call it a mistake. That's — the brush stopped. I noticed. Go on.
guarded|engaged|ask: All right. You're looking at the painting and not at the idea of me. Rare. Say the rest.
guarded|engaged|wild: That's yours. Not polished. I don't paint polished either.
guarded|engaged|*: Brush is in the air. Loaded. Don't make it mean anything.
engaged|engaged|path: Yes. Keep going. I can hold a brush and a thought.
That's right about the work. It's not yet about tonight.

engaged|wavering|path: …You respect the work. You didn't treat it as something in your way. Okay. Glasses off. It's late.
You talk about the painting like it matters. Most people talk about it like it's in the way.

engaged|wavering|ask: That's precise and it's kind and it's about the painting. I don't know what to do with that.
